eligibilityRule: Every documented callable in the selected published root entrypoint is implemented for its typed input domain with the same algorithmic work; all available upstream assertions plus added package-contract vectors pass; npm and LilScript app and isolated-workload checksums match; the LilScript port compiles to JavaScript, C, and a native executable; LilScript JavaScript is no larger than both npm/Vite and public-contract-preserving Closure ADVANCED in raw bytes or the selected Brotli-11 codec; and median isolated-workload throughput and retained memory are each no worse than 1.05x npm. Gzip-9 is reported as an alternate codec, not silently substituted into the configured gate.

ports.notes: This is the complete independently published @motionone/easing package. It is a Motion ecosystem component, not a claim that motion@13 is ported.
All documented numeric behavior is implemented. Invalid dynamic JavaScript values are rejected statically by LilScript rather than coerced at runtime.
The additional vectors verify BMP and surrogate-pair UTF-16 behavior.

The port preserves the package's prefix/suffix trimming, one-vector dynamic program, and UTF-16 code-unit behavior. Its function-local work array is verified as non-observable mutation by purity analysis.
The complete string-to-base36 API preserves upstream's explicit low/high 16-bit multiplication, typed signed bitwise operations, and unsigned radix serialization.

The published package contains no upstream test files. Eighteen fixed package-contract assertions cover both algorithms and the documented default murmur3 alias before dense differential vectors. Source-written Math.imul replaces the upstream low/high-half simulation without enabling compiler-introduced imul.

All eight exports and the adaptive floating-point expansion algorithms are source-equivalent to v3.0.3. The exact upstream suite is translated, including immutable commit-pinned hard fixtures verified by SHA-256; an additional deterministic corpus compares every result bit-for-bit with the installed npm package.

auditedButIneligible.reason: None of the seven published runtime entrypoints are implemented (1,028 entrypoint bindings / 546 unique names, including the 312-export root, DOM engine, and React surfaces); it remains context-only in the application lab.

The 6.0.1 package's conditioned root (five runtime exports with the pooled Node/Buffer algorithm) and two-export non-secure entrypoint remain unimplemented. The separate popular-library lab has an exact eligible port of the distinct nanoid 5.1.5 index.browser.js entrypoint only.

Its default class must preserve arbitrary JavaScript values and undefined, private non-enumerable linked-node state, enqueue/dequeue/peek/clear, the size getter, a live Symbol.iterator generator, and destructive drain generator. LilScript lacks exported private-field ABI and generator/yield support; a wrapper would add a second queue object and change allocations, so no size row is eligible.
